subject: environmental-science
title: Greenhouse Gases and Global Warming
welcome_lead: Track the radiative fingerprints of CO₂, CH₄, N₂O and HFCs.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on greenhouse gases and global warming potential.
final_note: Not all greenhouse gases are equal — methane's per-molecule punch dwarfs CO₂.

concepts.def: Re-radiation of infrared energy by atmospheric gases warming Earth's surface.
Cumulative radiative forcing of 1 kg of a gas relative to 1 kg CO₂ over 100 yr.
Methane; GWP ≈ 25 over 100 yr; sources include livestock, wetlands, gas leaks.
Nitrous oxide; GWP ≈ 298; major source agricultural soils.
Hydrofluorocarbons; refrigerants with GWPs up to ~14 000.
Net change in energy flux at the tropopause (W m⁻²) due to a perturbation.

walkthroughs.body_html: Polyatomic molecules with changing dipole moments absorb IR at characteristic wavelengths. CO₂ absorbs strongly at 15 μm.
CH₄ has a 12-yr lifetime but high near-term forcing. N₂O persists ~114 yr. Lifetime modulates GWP across time horizons.
Atmospheric CO₂ reached 420 ppm in 2023, up from 280 ppm pre-industrial. Total anthropogenic forcing now ~2.7 W m⁻².

mcqs.q: How do greenhouse gases warm Earth?
options: They absorb infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface and re-radiate some back down.
Because they generate too much energy.
They reflect sunlight back to Earth.
They block heat from escaping into space (like a literal lid).

mcqs.q: Why is ice-albedo feedback a positive feedback loop?
options: Because they generate too much energy.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Less ice means less reflective surface, so more sunlight is absorbed, causing more warming and more melting.
Because warming is positive (a good thing).

mcqs.q: Why does renewable energy require energy storage solutions?
options: Renewable energy can never meet demand.
They reflect sunlight back to Earth.
Solar and wind generation are intermittent - storage smooths out supply and demand.
Because they generate too much energy.
